values: Besides a dead-end street, « impasse » figuratively means a situation with no apparent solution.
In French geographical terminology, a « rivière » flows into another watercourse, while a « fleuve » reaches a sea or ocean.
For holidays or vacation time, French normally uses the plural « les vacances » and the expression « être en vacances ».
In entertainment and sport, « vedette » denotes a prominent star or featured person and remains grammatically feminine regardless of the person's gender.
The fixed expression uses the plural « enchères »; « vendre aux enchères » means to sell at auction.
« Vernissage » usually denotes the opening reception or preview of an art exhibition.
« Verre » can denote the material glass or a drinking glass; « un verre de » also denotes a glassful of a drink.
With time or quantities, « vers » means around or approximately; with movement, it means toward.
This compound color adjective is normally invariable: « des vestes vert olive ».
« Veuf » is masculine and « veuve » feminine; they refer to a person whose spouse has died and who has not remarried.

batch_summary: Added geographic distinctions, fixed-expression guidance, figurative senses, and agreement notes for common vocabulary.
